In the Deferred Acceptance algorithm, it is crucial to submit a truthful ranking of preferences because the algorithm is strategy-proof for students. This means that the best strategy for a student is to list schools in their true order of preference. Since the algorithm ensures that students are matched to the best possible option available to them, trying to game the system by misrepresenting preferences can lead to a less favorable outcome.

In this scenario, my preference order is w > y > x > z. My priority rank at school w and y is 1, meaning I am the highest priority candidate at these schools. Given that most applicants favor y > x > w > z, school y may be highly competitive. However, since I have the highest priority at both w and y, I should propose to my true top choice, which is w. If school w accepts me, I will be matched to my most preferred school. If not, I will propose to school y next, where I also have the highest priority.

Therefore, my best strategy is to submit my true preference order: w > y > x > z. This ensures that I am matched to the best possible school based on my preferences and priorities.
